narrative.overview: A late-evening listening room: dark wood shelving, cream sleeve labels, and one warm brass lamp that picks out what needs a hand. The interface is an operator console first. It is dense, tabular and calm, and the record-shop identity lives in a few precise places: the vinyl mark, the serif wordmark and page titles, and brass on the one thing the operator should act on next.
keyCharacteristics: Warm dark only; there is no light theme.
One accent (brass), used for action, selection, focus and progress.
Serif display face for the wordmark and page titles; a system sans for everything an operator reads or clicks.
Flat, bordered panels with tonal steps instead of elevation.
Status colour (red, amber, green, blue) is reserved for job and evidence state, always paired with a text label.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Brass marks the one thing to do next. If two brass fills sit side by side, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Label-With-Colour Rule
rules.body: State colour never stands alone: every red, amber, green or blue chip carries its word ("Failed", "Running", "2 to review").

rules.name: The Serif Is For Names Rule
rules.body: The display serif is for the wordmark and page and section titles only, never for buttons, labels, data or numbers.

rules.name: The Flat Shelf Rule
rules.body: Panels at rest have a border and no shadow.

dos: Do use the theme tokens (graphite-*, zinc-*, brass-*, muted, field-border) rather than raw hex in components.
Do keep one brass primary action per decision; make the rest secondary or text buttons.
Do give every screen one page title in the display serif.
Do keep the 2px focus-brass ring visible on every interactive element.
donts: Don't reintroduce blue-grey or neutral grey surfaces; the shelf is warm.
Don't use the serif on buttons, chips, numbers or table data.
Don't convey job or evidence state by colour alone.
Don't add shadows to panels at rest.
